acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Serpents family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Constrictor, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Space-Hold Soldier archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Long muscular snake with broad gripping belly scales, blunt wedge head, small teeth, and powerful midbody.
Signature mechanic: Anchored Coil: a completed tail loop tightens while the jaws maintain one visible anchor point.
battlefieldDuty: Loop around one obstacle or target and tighten only while its head remains anchored.
constructionDimensions: Ember seams appear between selected throat and belly scales while dorsal scales remain dark biological keratin.
Heat shimmer and narrow smoke lines follow the strike, venom lane, buried route, or tightening coil.
counterplay: Break the loop or stagger the anchored head to release all constriction pressure. Affinity signal: The loaded throat or anchor scale flares before release and exposes a cooling gap after the strike or constriction.
forbiddenTreatments: Flame that obscures coil boundaries or head position
identityInvariants: Every form remains limbless with a continuous scaled body, snake skull, jaw hinge, belly scutes, forked tongue, and species-appropriate tail.
Tier escalation uses body proportion, hood, fangs, horns, crown scales, muscle distribution, and coil behavior rather than arms or equipment.
Strike range, head anchor, venom direction, emergence point, and loosened coil remain visually traceable.
telegraph: The tail completes a circle and the jaw clamps firmly onto its anchor.
